question: How do Helium, Mimi, and Moshi's token streams work together to support full-duplex dialogue?
answer: Helium serves as a 7B-parameter text LLM backbone that provides strong reasoning abilities and linguistic knowledge to the system [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 7]. Mimi is a semantic-acoustic neural audio codec that uses residual vector quantization to encode audio into discrete units, allowing the model to produce high-quality speech while operating at low framerates compatible with real-time generation [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6]. These components are integrated into Moshi’s hierarchical multi-stream architecture, which models separate streams of semantic and acoustic tokens for both the user and the system, enabling the model to listen and speak simultaneously without explicitly modeling speaker turns [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 7]. Additionally, the Inner Monologue method generates text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens, allowing the speech-to-speech system to leverage Helium’s text-based knowledge while maintaining streaming inference capabilities [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 7].
